title: XYZ — Multi-Agent Coordination System
sources: ARCHITECTURE.md (relay stack map, verified against relay-drive.sh / relay-turn-lib.sh / *-turn.sh / poll.sh / bin/tick)
ROUTER.md (canonical entry points, subsystem routing hints)
README.md (two-layer model: tick kernel + relay-automation product)
repo directory structure: bin/, src/, relay-automation/, utils/pdda, utils/telemetry, utils/ate
utils/ate/SKILL.md + utils/ate/scripts/*.py (ATE: Gemma-driven Aider variation tester, folded in as its own subsystem)
utils/pdda/pdda.sh + pdda-gh-refresh.sh (gh issue list read path for issue-doc-sync)
legend_note: trust is a documentation-only annotation on top of the normal type/group fields — the swe-diagram renderer does not draw it specially. Vocabulary: trusted-primitive/trusted-orchestrator/trusted-dispatch/trusted-containment-core/trusted-supervisor = local, no independent code-execution authority of its own; untrusted-executor = an agent CLI running model-directed code, contained by something else, not by itself; sandboxed-worker = ATE's unattended local loop, no repo-write or network-credential authority of its own; external-credentialed = a real API key or a real GitHub side effect crosses here; shared-state = on-disk coordination surface, not itself a trust boundary; governance-gate = dev-time check, does not run during a live turn; runtime-audit = post-hoc verification, not a preventive control.

trust_boundaries.label: SAFETY BOUNDARY: untrusted agent-driven writes are contained by relay-lib, not by the agent itself
trust_boundaries.note: Every agent CLI (claude-cli/codex-cli/agy-cli/aider-cli) runs model-directed code with no independent sandboxing of its own. relay-turn-lib.sh is the actual boundary: path allowlist, worktree isolation at ROOT@HEAD, commit-bypass hard reset (exit 6), and timeout watchdog (exit 7) all live there, not in the model.

trust_boundaries.label: TRUST BOUNDARY: a shim only acts if RELAY_AGENT matches its own configured id
trust_boundaries.note: relay-drive.sh exports the current tick actor; every shim (claude-turn/codex-turn/agy-turn/aider-turn) checks RELAY_AGENT before doing anything and no-ops (exit 0) otherwise. This is what keeps four independently-invoked shims from ever racing each other for the same turn.

trust_boundaries.label: TRUST BOUNDARY: real API keys / real external side effects cross here
trust_boundaries.note: aider-cli reads its OpenRouter key from a local secrets file (never hardcoded). agy-cli's Google grounded search and ATE's gh issue create are the other two points in the whole suite where a real external credential or side effect is exercised.

trust_boundaries.label: SAFETY BOUNDARY (partial): post-hoc isolation-breach scan, not full containment
trust_boundaries.note: trust-audit scans agy's transcript for citations of the real repo root and fails the turn (exit 5) if found — but this detects one leak symptom, not full containment. A known false-positive gap is tracked in GH-183.

trust_boundaries.label: SAFETY BOUNDARY: only Claude, via checkin.py --abort, writes control.json
trust_boundaries.note: run_variations.py resets control.json to {action: continue} at the start of every run (killing stale aborts from a prior run). The unattended worker loop and the local Gemma classifier only ever read it, never write it.

trust_boundaries.label: SAFETY BOUNDARY (UNENFORCED): ATE's aider subprocess must stay inside a scratch repo
trust_boundaries.note: Unlike relay's worktree isolation — a real code-level guard — this is only an operational instruction in ATE's SKILL.md quick-start. Nothing in run_variations.py validates that --repo isn't the operator's real working tree. This is the one boundary in the whole suite that exists in docs but not in code.

trust_boundaries.label: TRUST BOUNDARY: local unattended loop -> exactly one external credentialed action
trust_boundaries.note: Regardless of how many hours ATE runs unattended, exactly one `gh issue create` call happens per run (or zero under --dry-run) — every intermediate result stays local in error_log.jsonl.

trust_boundaries.label: boundary: governance gates run outside the live agent-turn path
trust_boundaries.note: validate.sh and pdda.sh check correctness/doc-hygiene at dev time; neither runs during a live relay/marathon/ATE turn, so they can't stop an in-flight unsafe action — they gate before/after, not during.

nodes.label: tick CLI
nodes.description: The kernel: a local event-log CLI that hands out collision-free, path-scoped work claims (claim/scope/ping/release/done/cost). Answers 'whose turn is it?' via the RELAY-TURN task. No server, no API keys.

nodes.label: .tick/events log
nodes.description: Shared append-only event log serialized by an O_EXCL lock (src/lock.js). tick appends events and projects current task state (status/claimer/handoff-to) from them.

nodes.label: relay-drive.sh
nodes.description: Supervisor: reads tick + thread STATUS, derives the active actor, exports RELAY_AGENT/RELAY_FILE/RELAY_TASK, and invokes exactly one turn shim per round. Enforces round cap, no-progress (exit 3), and close-mismatch (exit 4).

nodes.label: relay-turn-lib.sh
nodes.description: Shared safety core: path allowlist, worktree isolation at ROOT@HEAD, timeout watchdog (rtl_run_bounded), commit-bypass guard (hard reset + exit 6), and one file-scoped commit — never pushes.

nodes.label: poll.sh
nodes.description: Hands-free decision engine for two live Claude windows: decides run-runner / watchdog / idle / stop / nudge-cross-model. tick decides whose turn is runnable; thread STATUS decides terminal.

nodes.label: marathon.sh
nodes.description: Chains several relay build->review phases in depends_on order from a MARATHON.yaml. The multi-agent coordinator built on the relay loop (marathon-drive.sh).

nodes.label: deep-research.mjs
nodes.description: Provider-agnostic grounded-search adapter. Spawns agy in print mode in a throwaway tmpdir, normalizes to {answer, citations, query, provider, model, raw}. Fail-closed typed errors, no silent fallback.

nodes.label: claude-turn.sh
nodes.description: Claude Code turn shim: pins the model, sets --allowedTools, shadows blocked commands on PATH, and captures token counts into tick cost. No-ops unless RELAY_AGENT matches.

nodes.label: codex-turn.sh
nodes.description: Codex turn shim: strips OPENAI_API_KEY unless allowed, runs 'codex exec -s workspace-write'. No-ops unless RELAY_AGENT matches.

nodes.label: agy-turn.sh
nodes.description: agy (Antigravity) turn shim: runs 'agy -p --dangerously-skip-permissions --print-timeout', treats exit-0-with-empty-log as a hard failure (exit 5). No-ops unless RELAY_AGENT matches.

nodes.label: aider-turn.sh
nodes.description: Aider <-> OpenRouter build lane. Owns tick token ops (Aider can't run shell mid-turn), asserts token ownership, runs Aider --no-auto-commits so the harness commits.

nodes.label: Claude Code CLI
nodes.description: Claude Code headless subprocess run inside the isolated worktree; edits the relay thread and moves the tick token.

nodes.label: Codex CLI
nodes.description: Codex headless subprocess; builds/reviews within the allowlist, moves the tick token via ./bin/tick.

nodes.label: agy CLI
nodes.description: Google Antigravity CLI. Serves both relay turns (build/review) and deep-research grounded search via its built-in Google search tool.

nodes.label: Aider CLI
nodes.description: Aider headless build runner using an OpenAI-compatible client; talks to models through OpenRouter. Two independent call paths: aider-turn.sh's relay lane (--no-auto-commits, harness commits) and ATE's run_variations.py, which spawns it directly per test variation against a scratch repo.

nodes.label: OpenRouter
nodes.description: OpenAI-compatible model gateway for the Aider lane (e.g. GLM 5.2, Nemotron), used by both the relay's aider-turn and ATE's variation grid. Key read from a local secrets file, never hardcoded.

nodes.label: Google grounded search
nodes.description: Google's grounded web search, reached through the agy CLI's built-in search tool; returns cited answers to deep-research.

nodes.label: GitHub (gh CLI)
nodes.tech: gh issue list / gh issue create
nodes.description: Shared external GitHub surface: pdda-gh-refresh.sh reads issue state (gh issue list) for the issue-doc-sync check; ATE's compile_issue.py writes exactly one rollup issue per run (gh issue create).

nodes.label: relay thread file
nodes.description: Human-readable review state: STATUS header (terminal signal) + per-turn review blocks. Holds review content, but NOT turn ownership (that is tick state).

nodes.label: XYZ.json + telemetry
nodes.description: Per-session completion feed appended by every relay/marathon/swarm session (harness/sessionId/health/title). Local + machine-specific; extractors read the event log.

nodes.label: control.json
nodes.description: ATE's only channel Claude writes to. run_variations.py resets it to continue at the start of every run so a stale abort from a prior run can't kill a fresh one; only checkin.py --abort writes an abort after that.

nodes.label: error_log.jsonl
nodes.tech: append-only JSON lines, one record per ATE variation
nodes.description: ATE's single source of truth. Every Aider variation appends here whether it passed or failed — the only artifact compile_issue.py reads to build the rollup.

nodes.label: validate.sh
nodes.description: Repo correctness gate: runs the full kernel + coordination test suite (Node 18+, no API keys). Must be green before reporting code/runtime success.

nodes.label: pdda.sh
nodes.description: Document-hygiene engine (PDDA contract): frontmatter, status-table, roadmap-coverage, changelog, stale, and issue-doc-sync checks over the PROJECT docs. issue-doc-sync reads cached GitHub issue state refreshed by pdda-gh-refresh.sh (gh issue list).

nodes.label: PROJECT docs + ledgers
nodes.description: PDDA-governed doc system: ROUTER/AGENTS entry points, ROADMAP pointer ledger, CHANGELOG record, and PROJECT/** execution docs (1-INBOX -> 2-WORKING -> 3-COMPLETED).

nodes.label: consult.sh
nodes.description: Parallel, read-only consult: fans the same question to Codex/agy/Aider in an isolated throwaway worktree and reconciles the answers into one. Mechanically stamps SINGLE-MODEL — NOT RECONCILED into the transcript when the panel degrades to one survivor (GH-178 A2).

nodes.label: Isolation-breach audit
nodes.description: Scans agy's transcript for citations of the real repo root and fails the turn (exit 5) if found, catching a grounding escape from the isolated worktree. Detects one leak symptom, not full containment — a known false-positive gap is tracked in GH-183.

nodes.label: run_variations.py
nodes.tech: Python, cycles variations.yaml grid unattended for --minutes
nodes.description: Owns ATE's loop: resets control.json to continue at start, checks it before every iteration, spawns aider-cli per variation, sends the result to Gemma for classification, appends one record to error_log.jsonl regardless of outcome, and chains to compile_issue.py at the end if --gh-repo was passed.

nodes.label: Gemma (LM Studio)
nodes.description: Classifies each Aider result (pass/fail, severity, category, likely_cause) via ask_gemma(). Has no filesystem or gh credentials of its own — only ever called with the last 1500 chars of stdout/stderr as text.

nodes.label: checkin.py
nodes.tech: Python, run by Claude every ~5 min
nodes.description: Claude's read side on the ATE run: tails error_log.jsonl and reports drift signals (repeated likely_cause, pass-with-traceback, staleness), and offers --abort "reason" as the one write path into control.json. Claude is the only actor with abort authority; it polls periodically rather than running unattended.

nodes.label: compile_issue.py
nodes.description: Chained automatically by run_variations.py the moment the run stops (time limit, abort, or the 20-pass safety cap), or run standalone for a manual rollup. Builds one severity-ranked checklist and is the only ATE component that calls gh issue create.

edges.label: resets to continue, polls each iteration
reads full log, groups by severity
